Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

items.headline: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

items.summary: Mayfield notched a season high in passing yards after finishing Tampa Bay's previous game without a completed pass, but he also threw multiple interceptions for the first time in six starts this season. He put forth a gutsy performance, getting back up from several big hits and scoring the game-tying two-point conversion with his legs to cap Tampa Bay's final drive, only for Chicago to kick a game-winning field goal on the ensuing possession. The struggling QB has taken a back seat to the Buccaneers' Bucky Irving-led running game in recent weeks, and Mayfield has an ugly 3:4 TD:INT heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye. items.headline: Titans WR Calvin Ridley involved in incident at Nashville airport

items.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

items.headline: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries.
items.summary: It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.headline: Michael Penix Jr. shows he could be Atlanta's QB1

items.headline: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
items.summary: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

items.headline: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.
items.summary: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.

items.headline: Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
items.summary: Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season. The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Jets just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.

items.headline: Kincaid (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's walk-through.
items.summary: Kincaid began last week with a limited session due to a chest issue, but was able to suit up for Monday night's win over the Vikings while seeing the field on 50 percent of the Bills' snaps on offense. In the process, the tight end caught all three of his targets for 28 yards. It's unclear if Kincaid's ankle injury occurred versus Minnesota or is something that occurred Wednesday, but either way added context regarding his status for this weekend's game against the Jets will arrive via Thursday's injury report.

items.summary: Latu gave the Bills the lead late in the first half when he got open in the back of the end zone and caught a pass from Josh Allen. It was not only his first catch of the campaign but also his first NFL touchdown. Latu has worked primarily on special teams this season, and despite his score Monday, he isn't likely to suddenly be a big part of the passing game given the fact that Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes all remain ahead of him on the tight-end depth chart.

It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.

items.headline: The Panthers designated Legette (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Just as head coach Dave Canales indicated earlier in the week would be the case, Legette will make his return to the practice field for the first time since Sept. 25. Legette, who has been sidelined for the Panthers' last six games while recovering from the knee injury, has a shot at being activated for Sunday's game against the Saints, though Carolina will have a full 21-day window to evaluate him for a return from IR. Once he's reinstated, Legette is likely to serve as the Panthers' No. 3 receiver behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker.

items.headline: Burden has a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson revealed after Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

items.headline: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.headline: According to coach Brian Schottenheimer, Ferguson (knee) is in line to miss multiple weeks, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

items.headline: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
items.summary: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.summary: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

items.headline: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

items.headline: Pickens (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Pickens maintained his activity level from last week, when he entered the weekend listed as questionable before the Cowboys included him among their inactives for this past Sunday's game at Indianapolis. Thus, he may need to get back to full Thursday and/or Friday to avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the 49ers.

items.summary: Watson repeatedly got the best of Christian Gonzalez and the rest of a talented Patriots secondary, recording team- and career-high receiving yardage totals along the way. Watson burned New England for four catches of 20-plus yards, including a game-long 49-yard grab, as well as a 39-yard touchdown reception in the latter portion of the third quarter. items.summary: Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. Stroud for a 63-yard TD in the second quarter. It was one of five touchdown passes for Stroud, who spread the ball around to nine different pass catchers and four that reached the end zone at least once. Dell will aim to build on the momentum next Sunday at Cleveland.

items.headline: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
items.summary: Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.headline: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
items.summary: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

items.headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Murray (hamstring) remains week-to-week, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Murray already has missed one game due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain and is expected to be sidelined longer as the Vikings begin prep for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, but O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to him as the team's Week 10 starting QB as of Wednesday. Assuming Murray is out again this weekend, Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer will be the signal-caller options at O'Connell's disposal.

items.headline: Vikings to start QB Carson Wentz against Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out
items.summary: Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out with a hamstring injury.

items.headline: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

items.headline: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

items.headline: Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

items.headline: Drake Maye digs the long ball: Patriots QB's success on deep passes keying surge
items.summary: After struggling on deep passes early, Maye has been one of the best in the league at producing chunk plays in the pass game over the past few weeks.

items.headline: Stevenson (knee) is absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of Patriots.com reports.
items.summary: Stevenson is expected to miss time after an early exit from Sunday's loss to the Packers. A Week 11 bye may or may not help him avoid a multi-game absence, but he's unlikely to play this Sunday in Munich against the Lions.

items.headline: Source: Pats' Rhamondre Stevenson expected to miss time with knee tendon issue
items.summary: Patriots top running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

items.headline: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland.
items.summary: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.

items.headline: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
items.summary: New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

items.headline: Five things Saints must fix entering Week 9 vs. Browns
items.summary: Protecting QB Tyler Shough, getting the run game going and igniting slow starts are among areas coach Kellen Moore is fixated on repairing.

items.headline: Likely caught five of six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: Likely finished two targets shy of Malik Nabers' team-leading total and one receiving yard shy of Darnell Mooney's team-best mark, but the TE scored the Giants' lone touchdown of the game. That TD came on a five-yard pass in the third quarter from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy (hip) for a drive and change before McCarthy returned to the game. Whether it's Winston or McCarthy under center, Likely projects to remain a key cog in the Giants' passing game for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, whose defense Likely carved up for 11 catches, 94 yards and two TDs in their Week 5 tie.

items.headline: Cooper (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.summary: Per  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic,coach Aaron Glenn downplayed Cooper's current ankle injury, noting of the wideout, "I think he'll he just fine." Meanwhile, Connor Hughes of SNY TV relays the that Cooper's current issue is affecting the same ankle that he hurt in Week 1.

items.headline: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

items.headline: Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

items.headline: McCaffrey rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: McCaffrey got banged up in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Falcons, but a Week 8 bye allowed his hamstring to heal, and the star running back handled 20 touches Sunday while scoring twice to bring his season total to 10 touchdowns. He capped San Francisco's opening drive with a one-yard touchdown run and added a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter. Rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black led the 49ers with 70 rushing yards on 11 carries, but McCaffrey remains the lead back heading into a Week 10 trip to Dallas, during which CMC will try to extend a seven-game touchdown streak.

items.headline: Nick Bosa back, Christian McCaffrey good to go for Niners
items.summary: The 49ers will have a healthy Nick Bosa for the first time since Week 2, and running back Christian McCaffrey is good to go this week against the Raiders.

items.headline: The key behind 49ers' 7-1 start? Big contributions from the team's youth
items.summary: While the 49ers' stars have shown out, Jordan Watkins, Jaden Dugger and Kaelon Black have also led the team to its best start since 2019.

items.headline: Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

items.headline: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
items.summary: The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

items.headline: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price have no game designations for Monday
items.summary: Seahawks running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price have no game designations, meaning both are healthy enough to play Monday night against the Bears.

items.headline: Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals.
items.summary: Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.

items.headline: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price have no game designations for Monday
items.summary: Seahawks running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price have no game designations, meaning both are healthy enough to play Monday night against the Bears.

items.headline: Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.

items.headline: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Bucs down Falcons without pass completion; Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell run wild
items.summary: Baker Mayfield didn't complete a pass, but the Buccaneers beat the Falcons 16-0 behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell's rushing on a wet, sloppy field.

items.headline: Where does Cam Ward stand coming out of the bye?
items.summary: Ward has nine games left to convince the Titans he should be their QB when they open the new stadium in 2027.

items.headline: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion.
items.summary: Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

items.headline: Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. He also gained 16 rushing yards on four carries and lost a fumble.
items.summary: The lost fumble was the first giveaway of the season for Daniels in six games. The third-year QB also struggled to sustain drives while working with a badly depleted wide receiver room, and his lone TD was a seven-yard toss to Van Jefferson -- a player who had zero catches on the year coming into Sunday -- in the second quarter. Injuries have derailed the first half of the season for the Commanders, but Daniels will try to spark his team to life in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.headline: Jayden Daniels, Commanders 'keep fighting through adversity,' improve to 2-4-1
items.summary: After falling behind 10-0 in the first half, quarterback Jayden Daniels led the Washington Commanders on a rousing rally, cruising to a 27-10 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Northwest Stadium, an effort in which he threw for 217 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Okonkwo (hip) was a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
items.summary: Now that he's gotten a full practice under his belt this week, Okonkwo should be in the clear for Thursday's game against the Giants. The veteran tight end has emerged a more integral part of the Washington passing game over the last four games, having cleared 70 percent snap shares in each of those contests while putting together a 19-218-0 receiving line on 24 targets.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Dissecting eight potential lineup conundrums for Week 9
items.summary: Breaking down the matchup upside and downside for Dak Prescott, Ashton Jeanty, Jonah Coleman, Nico Collins, Ladd McConkey, Omar Cooper Jr., Chig Okonkwo and Greg Dulcich.

items.headline: Williams caught three passes for 25 yards on six targets in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the year, Williams led the team's wide receivers and tight ends in snaps and routes against Los Angeles, but it was a tough matchup against a top-tier pass defense. Williams should have better games moving forward in one of the league's pass-happiest offenses. The rookie wideout should be a full-time player down the stretch in the second half of the season.

items.summary: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Aguilar off the Jaguars' practice squad Tuesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Arizona has yet to announce a corresponding move, but top quarterback Gardner Minshew could be headed to injured reserve after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks that may require season-ending surgery. An undrafted rookie out of Tennessee, Aguilar joins fellow rookie Carson Beck and veteran journeyman Josh Johnson as the healthy options in the Cardinals' quarterback room. Aguilar will likely settle in as the No. 3 option on the depth chart if Minshew is indeed placed on IR.

items.headline: Allgeier compiled 17 carries for 46 yards and caught two of three targets for no yards during Sunday's 17-3 defeat at Seattle.
items.summary: Allegeier has reeled off 10-plus touches in four straight contests, a span in which he's turned 65 touches into 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. He's been the beneficiary of repeated ankle injuries to rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, who must remain on IR for at least three more outings after Sunday's matchup, and the other current top RB on the active roster (Bam Knight) is in the concussion protocol, which will require clearance from an independent neurologist for his next game action. As a result, Allgeier is set up to retain a significant workload until Knight gets the all clear to return.

items.headline: Bowman reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Bowman was elevated to the active roster prior to Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks, failing to record any stats while playing four snaps with the special-teams unit. The tight end is eligible to be elevated one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: Duvernay registered two catches for eight yards on two targets, returned three kickoffs for 64 yards and brought back two punts for 21 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

items.headline: Fehoko was unable to haul in his lone target in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Fehoko has already climbed way up the wideout pecking order over the past two weeks, logging a 49 percent offensive snap share in both games after not exceeding a 12 percent snap share through the first seven weeks. However, the veteran wideout hasn't been able to do much with the recent opportunity, and he's stuck on one catch for 17 yards on two targets through nine contests. With that said, somebody is going to have to step up in the wideout corps to try to replace the production of Michael Wilson (neck), Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist), all of whom have been lost to season-ending injuries over the past two weeks. Fehoko is a candidate to take on some of that responsibility along with Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay and Harrison Wallace. The Cardinals will also be working with a new quarterback moving forward, as rookie Carson Beck is lined up to claim the starting role from Gardner Minshew (elbow), who landed on injured reserve Tuesday.

items.headline: Ford reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Ford was elevated to the active roster for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks, but he did not appear in the game. The running back could be elevated again in Week 10 versus the Rams if Bam Knight (concussion) remains sidelined.

items.headline: Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

items.headline: Hull failed to haul in his lone target during the Cardinals' 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.summary: Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Johnson will head to Arizona in what will mark the 15th different NFL organization that he's been a part of since entering the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008. The 40-year-old is expected to operate as the primary backup option behind rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who is poised to make his first NFL start Week 10 versus the Rams in place of the injured Gardner Minshew (elbow). With Minshew at risk of missing the remainder of the 2026 campaign while he recovers from a torn UCL, Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season concludes.

items.headline: Knight (concussion) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
items.summary: After suffering a concussion in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight wasn't able to practice last week before the Cardinals ruled him out ahead of this past Sunday's game in Seattle. With his return to drills this week, he's made progress through the protocol for head injuries, but the presence of the non-contact jersey indicates he's a few steps away from meeting with an independent neurologist.

items.headline: McBride recorded seven catches (on eight targets) for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle.
items.summary: With QB Jacoby Brissett getting traded to Baltimore this past week, McBride was on the receiving end of passes from Gardner Minshew, and the result was the tight end's fourth-fewest receiving yards in a game this season and also the fourth time he didn't reach the end zone through nine contests. On a positive note, McBride extended his streak with at least seven receptions to 11 outings, which matches the second-longest streak in NFL history, trailing only the 14 Antonio Brown put together from 2014-2015. McBride may have a tough task on his hands next Sunday against the Rams' surging defense.

items.headline: Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.summary: Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took some big hits in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Wallace from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.

items.headline: Arizona placed Bourne (tibia) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: Though Bourne is expected to avoid surgery after fracturing his right tibia during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys, he's facing an expected recovery timeline of three months that effectively ends his season. With Bourne heading to IR, the Cardinals signed Harrison Wallace off their practice squad to replenish their depth at receiver. The 31-year-old Bourne will finish the 2026 campaign with 26 receptions for 263 yards and no touchdowns on 38 targets over eight appearances.

items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Tuesday that Conner (foot) won't return from IR this week, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.

items.headline: The Cardinals designated Long (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday.
items.summary: The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.

items.headline: Dorsett signed with the Cardinals' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Dorsett has spent most of the past two seasons with Las Vegas' practice squad. He was cut Nov. 6 and has quickly found a new home with the Cardinals. Dorsett could be elevated as soon as this week, as Arizona is working with a depleted wideout corps after No. 1 option Michael Wilson (neck) joined Kendrick Bourne (tibia) on injured reserve Tuesday. However, Dorsett doesn't exactly have a recent history of success -- he hasn't logged an NFL regular-season snap since 2023 and hasn't caught a pass since 2022.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Jones to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Jones spent the final week of training camp with the Texans but was unable to crack the 53-man roster. He's now with the Cardinals as a member of the practice squad and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if Arizona was in need of depth at wide receiver. Jones played in eight regular-season games for the Cardinals in 2025 before being placed on injured reserve in mid-November due to an Achilles injury.

items.headline: Proche was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Proche was cut from the Browns' practice squad in mid-October, but he has now found another opportunity in Arizona. The wide receiver played in nine regular-season contests with the Titans in 2025, reeling in six of 12 targets for 65 yards, and he'll provide the Cardinals with an additional veteran depth option with Kendrick Bourne (tibia) expected to miss the rest of the year.

items.headline: The Cardinals placed Yeboah (undisclosed) on the practice squad injured list Tuesday.
items.summary: Yeboah reverted to Arizona's practice squad Monday after logging no offensive snaps and just 20 snaps on special teams. The 28-year-old is unavailable for at least the next four games after being placed on the practice squad IR. Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins still lead the way at tight end.

items.headline: Blair went without a target while playing nine of the Falcons' 53 offensive snaps in Sunday's 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Blair has been active for all eight of the Falcons' games this season, but the 29-year-old wideout has been scarcely involved on offense. He's thus far recorded just a six-yard reception on four targets, three of which came in Week 2. Blair should continue to suit up for the Falcons on gamedays but will provide most of his value on special teams.

items.headline: Coach Kevin Stefanski noted Monday that Branch (hamstring) won't play Sunday against the Bengals, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: The same applies to LB Samson Ebukam, with Josh Kendall of The Athletic relaying via Stefanski that either or both of the injured players could face multi-game absences. Through eight games thus far, Branch has caught 10 of his 12 targets for 64 yards. In the 2026 third-rounder's looming absence, Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus will continue to lead Atlanta's WR corps, with Chris Blair in reserve.

items.headline: Collins (hip) is listed as active Sunday against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

items.headline: Dalton is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals but was designated as his team's emergency third quarterback.
items.summary: As was the case in Week 8, Dalton will not occupy a roster spot Sunday, but he will be permitted to play should both Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa be forced from the game and unable to return.

items.headline: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

items.headline: Herbert carried the ball once for seven yards and caught two of his three targets for two yards during Atlanta's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: Herbert continued to serve a limited role in his first game since being signed to the active roster from the practice squad, as he played just 11 snaps on offense and nine on special teams. With Brian Robinson (hamstring) set to miss at least another three games, Herbert will likely continue to serve as the team's backup running back behind Bijan Robinson.

items.headline: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

items.headline: Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for five yards during the Falcons' 34-17 loss to the Bengals on Sunday in Madrid. He also returned one kickoff for 28 yards and returned two punts for minus-three yards.
items.summary: Zaccheaus briefly left Sunday's game and was evaluated for a possible concussion, but the veteran wide receiver was quickly cleared to return. He has only six catches (on 16 targets) for 26 yards through eight regular-season games, and he's caught one pass or zero in seven of those contests. Zaccheaus isn't a key piece in the Falcons' offense, and that's unlikely to change heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs on Nov. 15.

items.headline: Robinson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

items.headline: Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

items.headline: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

items.headline: Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
items.summary: Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

items.headline: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.
items.summary: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

items.headline: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
items.summary: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

items.headline: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Jacksonville but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Practice-squad elevation Austin Reed moved up to the No. 2 spot on the depth chart ahead of the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. While Slovis is inactive, he will be available if Reed and starter Joe Fagnano exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

items.headline: Wester went without a target while playing six of the Ravens' 51 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. He also returned three kickoffs for 71 yards and one punt for two yards.
items.summary: Though he remains locked in as the Ravens' top return man, Wester continues to see light playing time on offense. He hasn't logged double-digit snaps on offense since Week 3 and has been limited to four receptions for 44 yards on five targets through eight games.

items.headline: Randall (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
items.summary: Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.

items.headline: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets.
items.summary: Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings.
items.summary: Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

items.headline: Dortch went without a target while logging four of the Bills' 82 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He returned one kickoff for 22 yards and three punts for 40 yards.
items.summary: Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.

items.headline: Hawes caught his lone target for eight yards during Buffalo's win over the Vikings on Monday.
items.summary: Hawes played a season-high 46 snaps on offense and also played eight snaps on special teams. The 25-year-old has now caught a pass in consecutive games after failing to record any receptions across his first six outings of the campaign.

items.headline: Johnson rushed once for one yard and caught both of his targets for 36 yards against the Vikings in a 23-6 victory Monday.
items.summary: Johnson got just one carry while workhorse No. 1 RB James Cook logged a hearty 31 totes. However, Johnson made one big play as a receiver, hauling in a 36-yard reception on a third-down play early in the third quarter to bring Buffalo into Vikings territory. While Johnson has been nearly invisible as a ball carrier this season, he's been effective in a pass-catching role, racking up 210 yards on 17 catches through six games.

items.headline: Knox caught four passes for 37 yards on five targets in Monday night's 23-6 win over the Vikings.
items.summary: Knox's targets, catches and yards were all season highs. He also played 58 offensive snaps against Minnesota. With the blitz-happy Vikings defense opposite them, the Buffalo offense went with heavy tight end sets to try and get more blockers on the field. Knox won't be a recommended fantasy target for Sunday's game against the Jets. He has 13 grabs for 79 yards and a touchdown across eight games this season.

items.headline: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
items.summary: Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

items.headline: Palmer (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Monday, Joe Buscaglia of the Athletic reports.
items.summary: In Palmer's absence, DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman will lead the Bills WR corps Monday night against the Vikings, with Greg Dortch and Trent Sherfield available in reserve. The earliest that Palmer can return to the mix is Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Patriots.

items.headline: Shavers (knee) was not activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Monday night's matchup with Minnesota, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Shavers will remain sidelined for at least one more game as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL. The wide receiver returned to practice in late October, and he could be activated prior to the team's Week 10 matchup with the Jets.

items.headline: Sherfield reverted to the Bills' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Sherfield was elevated ahead of Monday's win over Minnesota and logged 10 snaps on offense along with 14 snaps on special teams. He did not otherwise get onto the box score. The veteran wideout has been elevated twice by Buffalo this season, so the Bills can elevate him once more before they'd need to sign him to the 53-man roster in order to deploy him on game day.

items.headline: Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.

items.headline: Dillon (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's battle against the Broncos, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: It's the third straight week that Dillon is a healthy scratch, and he hasn't logged game-day action since Week 4 against Detroit. Meanwhile, rookie RB Anthony Tyus continues to be active, due largely to his work as a kick returner. As such, it appears Dillon isn't likely to suit up unless one of the RBs ahead of him in the pecking order -- Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne or Tyus -- needs to miss time.

items.headline: Etienne carried the ball two times for seven yards and returned one punt for nine yards during Carolina'a loss Sunday to the Broncos.
items.summary: Etienne once again saw limited action offensively, playing just seven snaps. The 2025 fourth-round pick was the only running back other than Chuba Hubbard to record a carry and should continue to serve as the team's No. 2 back while Jonathon Brooks remains sidelined due to an abdomen injury.

items.headline: Evans caught both of his two targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-21 loss versus the Broncos.
items.summary: For the third game in a row, Evans drew exactly two targets and caught both of them Sunday. With that said, he also again trailed in snaps at tight end (31) behind teammates Tommy Tremble (46) and Darren Waller (35), both of whom also drew more targets in Week 9. Evans' role in the Panthers' passing offense isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats going into a Week 10 matchup at New Orleans.

items.headline: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver.
items.summary: The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.

items.headline: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as Carolina's emergency third quarterback Sunday against Denver, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: King should be used to this role, as it's one he's had in each of Carolina's contests so far  this season. It has yet to yield a regular-season snap for the rookie out of Georgia Tech, and King will be eligible to enter Sunday's matchup only if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

items.headline: Metchie caught both of his targets for 40 yards Sunday in a loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: Both of Metchie's receptions came in the second half -- he brought in a 15-yarder midway through the third quarter and added a 25-yarder near the end of the fourth. The latter catch took the ball down to Denver's nine-yard line and set up a Panthers touchdown, but Carolina ultimately was unable to complete the comeback. Metchie has been consistent but relatively unremarkable this season, logging either two or three receptions in six straight games but not surpassing Sunday's 40 yards in any of those contests.

items.headline: Sanders recorded zero targets during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: Sanders was active for the first time this season. However, he didn't log any offensive snaps and spent all his time on special teams. The 23-year-old has appeared in 30 regular-season games during his career, amassing 62 catches (77 targets) for 532 yards and two touchdowns. Sanders has had a few quality performances throughout his short NFL career, though he likely won't have an opportunity to get involved offensively moving ahead while Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are in the mix.

items.headline: Tremayne finished with an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Tremayne took the field for 19 of the Panthers' 73 snaps on offense, with his 26-percent share marking his lowest rate since Week 2. The 26-year-old appears to have been passed up on the depth chart at receiver by John Metchie, who logged 33 snaps Thursday and has now had higher playing-time shares than Tremayne for three straight games.

items.headline: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.

items.headline: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

items.headline: Brooks (groin) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
items.summary: Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 due to a groin injury that required core-muscle surgery and a stint on injured reserve. The Panthers designated him for return from IR on Wednesday, and he kicked off Week 10 prep with an uncapped walkthrough. How Brooks is listed on the injury report when Carolina holds practice Thursday and/or Friday may be the determining factor in his chances to play Sunday at New Orleans.

items.headline: Ahmed reverted to Chicago's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction report.
items.summary: Ahmed appeared in a game for the first time this season and carried the ball five times for 25 yards across his 17 offensive snaps in Sunday night's win over the Buccaneers. He could be elevated again for the Week 11 matchup versus the Saints if Kyle Monangai remains sidelined due to a knee injury.

items.headline: Chicago signed Carlson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Wednesday, Brendan Sugrue of USA Today reports.
items.summary: When Cole Kmet went to the Bears' injured reserve list with a season-ending knee injury following Week 7, it left the team with just two healthy tight ends on its active roster, so the move gives the club some much-needed depth at the position. As long as starter Colston Loveland and rookie third-rounder Sam Roush remain available, though, Carlson's role will likely be limited as the season progresses.

items.headline: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

items.headline: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Bears' emergency No. 3 quarterback for Sunday Night Football versus the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Keenum will once again operate as the team's emergency QB option in Week 9, making it four games in a row in that role. The 38-year-old will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent are forced out of the contest.

items.headline: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Monangai (thumb/toe) is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.

items.headline: Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

items.headline: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs.
items.summary: Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

items.headline: Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

items.headline: Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Swift was bottled up by an elite Buccaneers run defense that came into Week 9 allowing a league-low 80 rushing yards per game. He nearly had a fumble in the fourth quarter but was ruled down by contact on a play that the Buccaneers unsuccessfully challenged. Swift's momentum came to an abrupt halt with this season-worst performance, as he failed to reach 70 scrimmage yards for the first time all season after racking up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games. After Chicago's Week 10 bye, Swift could be back to sharing the backfield with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who hasn't played since Week 4 but recently returned to practice.

items.headline: Thomas hauled in one of his two targets for 13 yards and returned three kicks for 88 yards during Chicago's win versus Tampa Bay on Sunday.
items.summary: Thomas continues to see limited action offensively, playing just five snaps Sunday and no more than 15 on offense in any game this season, though he did manage to record his seventh reception of the season. The rookie third-round pick should continue to see the majority of his action come on special teams, and he's now amassed 715 kick-return yards across nine outings this season.

items.headline: The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
items.summary: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta.
items.summary: Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.

items.headline: Meyers caught two passes for 47 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.

items.headline: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out-produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a modest role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.

items.headline: Tinsley (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Tennessee.
items.summary: Tinsley has played in each of the Bengals' last three games and has logged four catches on eight targets for 56 yards over that span. He will observe Sunday's contest from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Falcons on Nov. 8.

items.headline: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.
items.summary: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.

items.headline: Head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Iosivas is doing well in his recovery from left thumb surgery, and the Bengals will "continue to work through this week" to determine when the receiver might return from injured reserve, Laurel Pfahler of the Dayton Daily News reports.
items.summary: Cincinnati has yet to open Iosivas' 21-day practice window since he landed on IR on Sept. 26, so until that happens, the wideout's return to game action shouldn't be considered imminent. While Iosivas has been sidelined for the Bengals' past six games, Dohnte Meyers has been serving as the primary No. 3 wideout behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and tight end Mike Gesicki has also benefited from an expanded profile in the passing attack.

items.headline: Bond went without a target while taking the field for eight of the Browns' 70 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.
items.summary: Since posting a 3-74-0 receiving line on seven targets in a Week 5 loss to the Jets, Bond has settled back into a muted role on offense. He's logged single-digit snaps in three straight contests, going without a target in each of those games.

items.headline: Boston isn't slated to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi reports.
items.summary: Boston logged a 93 percent snap share in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints, en route to hauling in six of his seven targets for 98 yards. However the rookie WR emerged from the contest with a toe issue that will make his status worth watching ahead of this weekend's game against the Texans. If Boston -- who's expected to return to practice Thursday, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer -- ends up being available, he'll be catching passes once again from Deshaun Watson, while Week 9 starter Shedeur Sanders will revert to serving as the Browns' QB2.

items.headline: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry.
items.summary: Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders.
