items.headline: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
items.summary: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

items.headline: Price caught one of his four targets for six yards in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo on Monday Night Football. He also gained 12 yards on one punt return and brought back four kickoffs for 124 yards.
items.summary: Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Claiborne (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

items.headline: The Vikings released Beckham on Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Signed off the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against the Bills, Beckham made his Vikings debut in the 23-6 loss, going without a target while playing just two snaps on offense. He'll end up giving up his spot on the 53-man roster just one day later after the Vikings brought in quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders prior to the deadline, but Beckham won't be without a home for long. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Beckham is expected to re-sign with the Vikings' practice squad and will be eligible to be elevated for three more games.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Briscoe (undisclosed) on their practice squad injured list Wednesday.
items.summary: It's not immediately clear exactly what happened, but as a result of the move, Briscoe will not be eligible for elevation to the active roster for Minnesota's next four games. He's still waiting to make his regular-season debut since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in May.

items.headline: Minnesota signed Culp to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Just a little more than a week after getting cut from the Browns' practice squad, Culp has now found another opportunity with a new club. He suited up for 13 games with the Buccaneers in 2025, catching his only target for six yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Lauter to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding moves, the Saints also signed tight end Treyton Welch to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Lauter started with the Raiders as an undrafted free agent during the offseason and is still waiting to make his regular-season NFL debut.

items.headline: Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

items.headline: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.
items.summary: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

items.headline: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams.
items.summary: Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

items.headline: Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

items.headline: New England signed Jennings to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Jennings is a familiar face for the Patriots, as he suited up for 10 regular-season games with them over the last two campaigns, taking 36 carries for 106 yards and a touchdown. With 2025 second-rounder TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an illness that sidelined him in Week 8, New England is understandably looking to add some organizational depth in its backfield.

items.headline: Miller reverted to the Patriots' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: The wide receiver was elevated for New England's Week 8 win over Miami after the team ruled out A.J. Brown (knee/ankle). Miller saw action on five offensive snaps but did not record a catch. Brown's status next week could go a long way toward determining whether Miller is elevated again.

items.headline: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
items.summary: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

items.headline: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: With Donaldson out and Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve, the Saints will roll with a three-man backfield of Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime. One of the league's least productive backfields doesn't evoke much fantasy excitement.

items.headline: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland.
items.summary: The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties at the position. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
items.summary: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.headline: Kamara (rest/back) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: The Saints backfield is in a bit of flux at the moment, with Kamara and CJ Donaldson (shoulder) logging DNPs on Wednesday and Travis Etienne (hamstring) closing on a return from injured reserve. At the moment, Audric Estime is the healthiest option at the position, and he and Kamara Split the RB reps during this past Sunday's win against the Browns, with Kamara earning a 49 percent share share and turning nine touches into 49 yards from scrimmage, while the former logged 47 percent of the snaps and had 16 touches for 77 total yards and one rushing TD. Kamara was listed with rest and back last Wednesday, so his DNP to start the week likely is more of a veteran rest day than anything.

items.headline: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
items.summary: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

items.headline: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
items.summary: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

items.headline: White reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With Travis Etienne (IR, hamstring) still sidelined and Kendre Miller cut over the weekend, White was elevated as the RB3 behind Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime. White played four offensive snaps against Cleveland on Sunday and rushed one time for five yards.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: The former Jet remains the odd-quarterback out for the Saints. Wilson will not be allowed to play in Sunday's contest unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints will wait until the end of the week to make a decision whether or not to activate Etienne from injured reserve, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: Considering Etienne went down as a limited practice participant Wednesday, the Saints have officially designated him for return from injured reserve, where he's resided since his last appearance in Week 3 when he suffered a left hamstring strain. He's missed the last five games as a result, but for him to have a chance to play Sunday against the Panthers, the team will need to activate him from IR by Saturday afternoon.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Welch to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding transactions, the Saints also signed tight end Matt Lauter to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Welch has already suited up for five games with New Orleans this season, with most of his snaps coming on special teams.

items.headline: Desrosiers carried the ball three times for 20 yards during the Giants' win over the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Desrosiers made his regular-season debut during the victory, serving as the team's No. 2 running back behind Devin Singletary, as Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury. With Skattebo now healthy again, Desrosiers will likely be relegated to a depth role during Thursday's matchup versus the Commanders.

items.headline: Fidone (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's contest in Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Fidone suited up for each of New York's previous three games before a Week 8 bye, but he's a healthy scratch against the Eagles. The second-year tight end has worked mostly on special teams this season and has one catch for 29 yards on one target over three contests. Fidone figures to be at risk for inactive status when the three tight ends ahead of him in the pecking order -- Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz -- are healthy.

items.headline: Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: The rookie wideout is a distant third in the pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.

items.headline: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

items.headline: Johnson wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: The tight end played just 12 offensive snaps, logging a 17.9 percent snap share against Philly. On the season, Johnson has just four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown on nine targets across six appearances. He has no fantasy appeal with Isaiah Likely healthy.

items.headline: Jones (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Jones was limited throughout Week 9 prep with a thumb injury. The wide receiver is not only active but was not wearing a cast or brace over the injured appendage as he fielded punts in pregame warmups.

items.headline: Mafah reverted to the Giants' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With both Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Tyrone Tracy (IR, hamstring) sidelined, Mafah joined Greg Desrosiers as the healthy running backs behind Devin Singletary. Mafah played just 10 snaps on special teams and none on offense Sunday against Philly.

items.headline: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

items.headline: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.

items.headline: The Giants signed Gray to their practice squad Monday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Gray is back with the organization that drafted him back in 2023 after spending some time early in the season on the Browns' practice squad. With Cam Skattebo dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a chance Gray could end up being elevated to the active roster for the Giants' contest at Philadelphia in Week 9.

items.headline: The Giants signed Haener to their practice squad Saturday,Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Haener has been part of New York's active roster twice this season, and he was most recently waived by the team Thursday. The Fresno State product will remain in the organization on the practice squad, as the Giants have J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston as their quarterbacks on game days. Should one of those two get injured and need to miss time, Haener figures to be elevated or signed to the roster again.

items.headline: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

items.headline: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

items.headline: Nwangwu was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Nwangwu remained inactive for the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins despite logging a full practice Friday. The running back has returned to form for Week 8 prep and should be all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

items.headline: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

items.headline: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
items.summary: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

items.headline: Patrick is inactive (coach's decision) for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.summary: Garrett Wilson is sitting out due to a concussion, but Patrick still won't suit up for Sunday's contest. The 32-year-old has been a healthy scratch the past two weeks after catching three passes for 41 yards in the previous three games.

items.headline: The Jets signed Manjack to the practice squad Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie receiver out of TCU had previously spent time with Denver in the offseason, appearing in all three preseason games while catching three of four targets for 40 yards. After failing to make the Broncos' roster heading into Week 1, Manjack had been a free agent before landing an opportunity with the Jets.

items.headline: Brown recorded one catch for 16 yards on one target Sunday in a loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Brown logged 35 offensive snaps, well behind fellow wideouts Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper (65 snaps apiece). The Eagles were without both DeVonta Smith hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for the third straight week, but Brown hasn't done much in their absences, tallying just five catches for 63 yards on eight targets during that span. Philadelphia is on bye for Week 10, and if Smith and/or Wicks return for Week 11 versus Pittsburgh, Brown's role figures to decrease.

items.headline: Covey (knee) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Giants.
items.summary: Covey was again unable to practice during the week because of the knee injury he suffered back in Week 7 versus the Cowboys, and he'll miss his second straight game in Week 9. In his absence, 2025 fifth-rounder Jaydon Blue and 2024 second-rounder Cooper DeJean will likely continue to see increased opportunities in the return game.

items.headline: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

items.headline: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
items.summary: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

items.headline: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

items.headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: The Eagles released Pierce (undisclosed) from IR with an injury settlement Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.summary: Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another organization.

items.headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: Smith thus will sit out for the fifth time in six games due to a hamstring injury. Fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also won't play Sunday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to man the Eagles' receiving corps. Smith's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 22, versus the Steelers.

items.headline: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

items.headline: Wicks (ankle) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: After sitting out practice Friday, Wicks will miss a third straight game for Philadelphia. He'll now have the team's Week 10 bye to try and get right coming out of the break. The Eagles will continue to roll with Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper as their Nos. 1 and 2 receivers against New York this week.

items.headline: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
items.summary: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

items.headline: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

items.headline: Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown.
items.summary: With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

items.headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency third quarterback against the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: Howard will continue to operate as the emergency QB3, which means he is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

items.headline: Skowronek (calf) is inactive against the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: Skowronek will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a calf injury, and with the Steelers on a bye for Week 9, his next chance to play is Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kaden Wetjen, Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson are in line for more snaps on offense in Skowronek's absence.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Smith off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.

items.headline: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
items.summary: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

items.headline: Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns.
items.summary: Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

items.headline: Pittman (foot) is making progress but won't have his practice window opened this week, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Pittman resumed running in late October and could resume practicing at some point in November. It won't happen this week, however, leaving the Steelers with minimal WR depth beyond DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

items.headline: Johnson reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Johnson's third consecutive elevation to the active roster resulted in his first target and catch of the season, which netted  nine yards. The wide receiver will now need to be signed to the 53-man roster to suit up for the Steelers in any future 2026 regular-season contests.

items.headline: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense figures to decrease with Keenan Allen now in the fold, and with Evans or Samuel potentially ready to return.

items.headline: Evans (Achilles) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
items.summary: The veteran wideout's absence Wednesday isn't surprising, with Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site having previously reported that Evans is not expected to be ready this week, with the caveat that the team will continue to evaluate his status in the coming days. In other 49ers' WR news, Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was able to log a limited practice Wednesday, while the team added valuable depth at the trade deadline by inquiring Keenan Allen from the Colts.

items.headline: Hodge reverted to the 49ers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With the Niners still dealing with several injuries at wide receiver, Hodge appeared in his fourth game this season and played 12 offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Raiders. He caught his lone target for 17 yards and has two grabs for 35 yards this season.

items.headline: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas.
items.summary: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

items.headline: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries in Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
items.summary: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders prior to the deadline.

items.headline: Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. He added seven rushing attempts for 40 yards and a touchdown.
items.summary: Purdy gave the 49ers a 14-0 lead with a one-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, then added a 12-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey in the second quarter and a 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins in the third. Unfazed by the numerous injuries to San Francisco's wide receivers, Purdy has a 17:5 TD:INT through the air to go with a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Cowboys. Having led the 49ers to a 7-1 record, the fourth-place finisher in the 2023 MVP race is making a strong case for the award at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Samuel (hamstring) will return to practice Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard reports.
items.summary: This will mark Samuel's first on-field work of any kind since he suffered a right hamstring injury during a Week 5 win at Seattle, and he'll officially go down as a limited participant, per Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area. Samuel likely will need to string together multiple practices this week to feel comfortable clearing him to play Sunday in Dallas.

items.headline: The 49ers placed Kirk (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Kirk made his season debut in San Francisco's last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, going without a target on a 30 percent snap share. After a Week 8 bye, he showed up on the initial Week 9 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a knee injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to be to the wide receiver's meniscus Friday, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com. Shanahan also relayed that Robinson may need surgery, but at the very least he'll miss the team's next four contests.

items.headline: Stribling (ankle) was spotted Monday walking without crutches or a brace on his lower leg, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

items.headline: Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown.
items.summary: Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

items.headline: Foster reverted to the Seahawks' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Foster logged his first career regular-season offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Cardinals but didn't touch the ball on five plays he was in for. He's appeared in three contests for Seattle this season, seeing 10 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona.
items.summary: Holani logged just two offensive snaps, by far his lowest count in a game of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson also is on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all in Week 10.

items.headline: Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.

items.headline: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

items.headline: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
items.summary: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

items.headline: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

items.headline: The Seahawks released Jones on Friday, Howard Balzer of USA Today reports. He was then signed back to the team's practice squad, per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com.
items.summary: Jones has been dealing with a hamstring injury and was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday after missing Monday's loss to the Bears. He didn't appear on the practice report Friday because Seattle decided to let the veteran running back go. However, Jones agreed to re-sign as part of the club's practice squad later in the day, so he'll now serve as depth in case injuries strike the Seahawks' running-back room again.

items.headline: The Seahawks signed Martinez to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: With Sam Darnold (quad) week-to-week, Martinez gives Seattle another body at quarterback. He logged one regular-season snap with San Francisco last season.

items.headline: Seattle signed Sims to its practice squad Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.summary: Seattle tried out Sims on Tuesday, and the team evidently liked what it saw enough to bring him on as a member of the practice squad. Over 11 games with the Packers and the Vikings in 2025, he caught three of six targets for 30 yards.

items.headline: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

items.headline: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
items.summary: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

items.headline: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

items.headline: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.

items.headline: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
items.summary: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught three of five targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Ayomanor's role didn't grow much, as Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm and Chimere Dike combined to see 22 of the team's 39 targets. Through eight games this season, Ayomanor has 13 grabs for 211 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets.

items.headline: Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Dike receiving the biggest playing-time boost on offense, as he ran 40 routes on Cam Ward's 46 dropbacks. Only Gunnar Helm produced more receiving yards than Dike in the Week 8 defeat, and only Wan'Dale Robinson (six) recorded more catches. With the Titans headed into their Week 9 bye, Tate figures to be back the following week versus Jacksonville. Perhaps Dike can earn more playing time at Elic Ayomanor's expense, and Calvin Ridley's name has been linked to trade speculation.

items.headline: Granson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: The sixth-year tight end will be a healthy scratch for a third consecutive game and the sixth time this season. The Titans are on a bye for Week 9, so his next opportunity to suit up is Week 10 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 15. That said, Granson is unlikely to see the field unless there is an absence ahead of him on the tight end depth chart.

items.headline: Helm caught five of nine targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Helm led the team in targets while he was able to register a new career-high 76 receiving yards in the contest. The tight end has now reeled in eight passes over the last two weeks after he caught nine of 13 targets for 60 yards over the first six games of the 2026 campaign. Helm will have a tough test against the Jaguars in Week 10 after the team's bye week in Week 9.

items.headline: Sources: Giants called Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson before trade deadline
items.summary: The Giants made a call to the Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.

items.headline: The Titans opted not to move Pollard ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, despite him drawing interest from teams, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Given his standing as a 29-year-old running back on an expiring deal for a 1-7 team, Pollard looked to be a natural candidate to be dealt at the deadline. The Titans instead opted to keep Pollard around, perhaps with the hope of coming to terms with him on a contract extension before he hits free agency. Though he's taken a step back in the passing game in 2026 with a 14-70-0 receiving line through eight games, Pollard is in the midst of the best of his three seasons in Tennessee as a rusher. He's churned out 595 yards and six touchdowns on 133 carries, which includes 100-plus-yard rushing efforts in both of his last two outings.

items.headline: Robinson caught six of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Robinson didn't experience a significant change in role in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder), as this was the fourth consecutive game in which Robinson notched either six or seven targets. His 57 receiving yards tied a season high, and Robinson scored his third touchdown of the season on a 15-yard catch in the fourth quarter. The Titans took a seven-point lead with 3:46 remaining after a successful two-point conversion following Robinson's TD, but the Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown drive and eventually won in OT to drop the Titans to 1-7. Robinson and the Titans will be on bye in Week 9 before returning to action against the Jaguars in Week 10.

items.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that Singleton is "getting better," and the rookie running back could be a candidate to see added opportunities in the second half of the season if lead back Tony Pollard is dealt ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: A fifth-round pick out of Penn State, Singleton was a healthy inactive for four of the Titans' first eight games prior to a Week 9 bye and has logged more snaps on special teams than offense thus far during his rookie season. However, with the 29-year-old Pollard set to become a free agent after the season and likely not part of the 1-7 Titans' rebuilding effort, playing time could become up for grabs in the backfield if Tennessee receives an appealing trade offer for the veteran. Along with Singleton, Tyjae Spears (knee) and Michael Carter would be vying for reps in the event Pollard is traded, while Julius Chestnut is another option in the backfield but has been utilized almost exclusively on special teams.

items.headline: Spears (knee) didn't practice Wednesday.
items.summary: Spears missed the last two games before Tennessee's Week 9 bye. Between the lingering knee injury and the reality that Tony Pollard wasn't traded before the deadline, Spears faces a difficult path to relevance in the second half of the season.

items.headline: Tate (shoulder) won't practice Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.summary: Tate last saw game action in Week 7, but Paul Kuharsky of PaulKuharsky.com previously suggested that the wideout was expected back after the Titans' Week 9 bye. However, a 'DNP' on Wednesday for Tate isn't a good sign. That said, he still has two more chances to  resume practicing ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

items.headline: Restrepo reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: All 19 of Restrepo's snaps in Week 8 came on special teams, and he recorded two solo tackles in that phase. With rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate (shoulder) expected back after Tennessee's bye in Week 9, Restrepo's path to snaps at wide receiver will likely remain non-existent.

items.headline: Bates (shoulder) is active for Sunday night's matchup with the Eagles.
items.summary: Bates was dealing with a shoulder injury throughout the week, but he'll ultimately be able to give it a go for Sunday Night Football. He'll operate as a depth option behind Chig Okonkwo and Ben Sinnott at tight end versus Philadelphia.

items.headline: Bradley reverted to the Commanders' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Bradley appeared in his first career regular-season game in Sunday's loss to the Rams, recording one catch for 12 yards across 17 offensive snaps. He could get some more run in the coming weeks if Dyami Brown (calf) remains sidelined for Washington.

items.headline: Burks (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Giants.
items.summary: Despite logging DNPs Monday and Wednesday, Burks is good to go after getting in a limited session Tuesday. He missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams but figures to return to his role in three-wide sets alongside rookie Antonio Williams and veteran slot man Stefon Diggs, which would push Van Jefferson down the depth chart after he popped up for 5-58-1 receiving against Los Angeles. Burks has produced seven catches for 147 yards on 11 targets over his last two games with Terry McLaurin (knee) sidelined.

items.headline: Diggs caught three of five targets for 51 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo ended up leading the Commanders' injury-depleted group of pass catchers with seven targets each, and the former led the team in receiving yards and caught Jayden Daniels' only TD pass. Diggs' modest showing still represented his biggest yardage total since Week 1, although he did see his two-game scoring streak come to an end. Diggs will try to ramp up his production in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.headline: Ekeler rushed eight times for 16 yards and caught two of three targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Ekeler led the team in carries, toting the rock one more time than fellow running back Rachaad White in the loss. Ekeler also was able to reel in multiple passes for the second time in three games, and he figures to remain in a relatively even backfield split with White against the Giants in Week 10.

items.headline: The Commanders claimed Henry off waivers from the Seahawks on Tuesday.
items.summary: After being cut by Seattle on Monday, Henry quickly caught on with the Commanders. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA had previously joined the Commanders for training camp and the preseason, only to be waived prior to Week 1. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve for at least two more games and Jeremy McNichols (foot) likely to miss the remainder of the season, Henry will provide the Commanders with another option in the backfield behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler. Henry didn't end up making his NFL debut during his time on the Seahawks roster.

items.headline: Jefferson caught five of seven targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: With Terry McLaurin (knee) and Treylon Burks (foot) out for the Commanders, Jefferson played 36 of 62 offensive snaps and ran 25 routes on Jayden Daniels' 42 dropbacks. The veteran wideout was signed to the active roster from the practice squad two weeks ago and led the team in receiving against Los Angeles. If Burks needs to miss more time, Jefferson could again have a role in three-wide sets Thursday night against the Giants.

items.headline: Kaliakmanis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles but will serve as the emergency No. 3 quarterback.
items.summary: The rookie seventh-round pick will continue to operate as Washington's third quarterback behind Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota. Both QBs would need to be forced out of the game for Kaliakmanis to see the field.

items.headline: Mariota (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Mariota was sidelined for the previous two games with a sprained MCL but is ready to resume QB2 duties coming out of the Commanders' bye. Athan Kaliakmanis should slide back down to the QB3 spot for Washington.

items.headline: White carried the ball seven times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: The 28 rushing yards led the Commanders on the afternoon, although Austin Ekeler saw one more carry than White did. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) set to miss at least one more contest while on IR, White seems likely to lead the backfield again in Week 10 against the Giants. Over the three games Croskey-Merritt has been sidelined so far, White has produced 186 scrimmage yards and two TDs -- one rushing and one receiving -- while averaging 4.4 yards per carry.

items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn ruled out Yankoff (knee) for Thursday night's games against the Giants, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports.
items.summary: Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not assumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

items.headline: The Commanders placed Brown (calf) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

items.headline: McLaurin (knee) underwent surgery Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.

items.headline: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.
